title: 2025 年河南中考英语
source: 2025年河南中考英语试题及参考答案
note: 听力1—20题未收；22题图片选项已转为对应食物文字；逐页对照扫描原卷补齐文字层缺失内容。

groups.label: A
groups.title: 有机食品市集
groups.passage:
COMMUNITY ORGANIC FOOD MARKET
After the great success of last year’s Community Organic (有机的) Food Market (COFM), this year’s COFM will be bigger and better. Food stands include:
Aunt Joy’s Organics: Home-grown organic apples and vegetables from Aunt Joy’s own garden. Special offer: 30% off.
Grace’s Honey (蜂蜜): Nature’s sweet treat collected by Grace herself. 100% natural honey!
Cornfield Bakery: Handmade organic bread. Special offer: Two for the price of one!
Lucy’s Kitchen: Organic vegetable hamburgers and fruit pizzas. The only stand that serves food to take away.
Notes: Bring your own reusable bag and remember to “travel green” (No parking lots). Tickets will only be sold on the day. All the money goes to our vegetable garden project. Price: £5 for one ticket. Free for children under 7. There’s no card machine, so please bring cash. It’s a good idea to come early.
COFM will be open 10:00 A.M.—5:00 P.M. on July 6, in Town Square. JOIN US! Enjoy a taste of organic lifestyle!

items.stem: Which stand sells takeaway food at COFM?
items.exp: Lucy’s Kitchen 是唯一卖外带食物的摊位。

items.stem: Which of the following is on the special offer “buy one and get one free”?（原图片选项转为文字）
items.exp: Cornfield Bakery 的 two for the price of one 即买一赠一，原图为面包。

items.stem: What is a COFM-goer advised to do?
items.exp: 公告倡导绿色出行且没有停车场，应避免开车。

items.stem: How much should they pay if a 6-year-old boy and his parents go to COFM?
items.exp: 每张票5英镑，7岁以下免费，两名成人共10英镑。

items.stem: What is the text?
items.exp: 公告介绍活动信息、号召参与，是海报。

groups.label: B
groups.title: 每个人都有自己的天赋
groups.passage: “Stephen!” shouted Billy from the back of the class. "What's 160 divided by 7?" "22.85714," replied Stephen without looking up. “Good job!” said Billy, copying the number down in his notebook.  "Stephen! When is Thomas's birthday?" asked Mary. "It's February 16," said Stephen, "and he was born on a Tuesday." "Wow!" said Thomas. "How did you know that?" "You told me," said Stephen, "on November 5 last year, at 3:05 pm. It was nine months, three days, four hours and sixteen minutes ago...” Carol cut in, "You did the calculation (计算) all in your head?" "Yes, of course," said Stephen. "How else would I have done it?" Carol couldn’t believe her ears and almost fell off her chair. "Wow!" said Thomas. "We have a real genius (天才) here. Right here, in our class!” He looked at Stephen and gave him a big smile. Stephen turned bright red, like a tomato. "I am not a genius," he said quietly. "I'm just Stephen. " "But you're so good at math and remembering things, surely you must be a genius," said Thomas kindly. "I can prove I'm not," said Stephen. He got up and started to collect things from his classmates: a painting, a geography notebook, a history notebook and an English notebook. Then he went to the front of the class. "Tell me what you see," Stephen said, holding up Carol's painting. "A really good picture!" shouted out Thomas. Next Stephen picked out Thomas’s geography notebook. "Listen up," he said. "Test 1, A+. Test 2, A+. Test 3, A+." "Good job!" Mary shouted. "Now you, Mary," said Stephen. "History project last term — teacher's words: an excellent piece of work. History project last year — teacher's words: excellent, good job, Mary." Stephen continued, "Now I'm going to read you a poem." It was from Billy's English notebook. "What a beautiful poem!" said Carol. "And what a nice way to prove you're not a genius," said Thomas. "You just showed us that ▲, didn’t you?" "I hope so," said Stephen, and he went back to his desk without another word.

items.stem: How was Stephen’s special ability shown at the beginning of the story?
items.exp: 开头通过回答同学的问题展示计算与记忆能力。

items.stem: How might Carol be feeling when she almost fell off the chair?
items.exp: Carol 不敢相信耳朵，几乎跌下椅子，说明惊讶。

items.stem: Which subject was Mary good at?
items.exp: Mary 的 history project 得到优秀评价。

items.stem: Which of the following can be put in ▲?
options: it’s very important to learn math well
it’s no use being a genius at all
we’re all geniuses in our special ways
we are much smarter than you
items.exp: Stephen 列举每位同学的长处，说明人人有自己独特的天赋。

items.stem: What can we learn about Stephen?
options: He was smart but not proud.
He was good at telling stories.
He was hard to get along with.
He was used to copying others.
items.exp: 他能力突出却否认自己比别人特殊，体现聪明而不骄傲。

groups.label: C
groups.title: 阳光的科学
groups.passage: Sunshine does make people happier. Imagine how cheerful you are when it clears up after long cold rainy days. Let's discover science behind sunlight. Sunlight causes you to produce a chemical called serotonin (血清素). When you are exposed to sunlight, your body will make more serotonin. Higher levels of serotonin will keep you in good spirits. At night, when there is little or no light, your body produces another chemical — melatonin (褪黑激素). It helps your body relax and will make you feel tired, which can prepare you for a good night's sleep. You should keep a good balance between these two chemicals. However, for many people, it is hard to balance sunlight with darkness. People who stay indoors a lot may not get enough sunlight. The light in a house is usually about 100 times less than that outside on a sunny day. That's why it is believed that those people should get outside in the sunshine. They can get some exercise, enjoy the fresh air and be happy, all at the same time.  There are places where it gets dark for a long time in the winter. People in those places are easier to get seasonal affective disorder (SAD). People with SAD usually go through bad experiences such as low energy and sadness. The most common treatment for those people is to sit under bright artificial (人工的) lights for some time. The roles that sunshine plays in people's life are more than those above. For example, your body produces Vitamin D (维生素D) from sunlight, which is important for being healthy. In fact, there is more science about sunlight for you to discover. So next time, when you notice the sunshine on your shoulder, take a moment to think, “Why do we love sunshine?”

items.stem: Which of the following can take the place of “are exposed to” in the text?
items.exp: 暴露在阳光下即待在阳光中，用 stay in。

items.stem: What does Paragraph 2 mainly talk about?
options: What can help people to keep in good spirits.
How light influences people through chemicals.
Why melatonin can help people relax for a sleep.
Which chemical is thought to be more important.
items.exp: 第二段讲光照通过血清素和褪黑激素影响情绪与睡眠。

items.stem: Which of the following is an opinion according to the text?
options: There are places where it gets dark for a long time in the winter.
People who stay indoors a lot should get outside in the sunshine.
The light in a house is usually less than that outside on a sunny day.
People’s bodies produce something called Vitamin D from sunlight.
items.exp: should get outside 是作者给出的主张，其他选项是可核实的事实。

items.stem: Jack is a person with SAD. How could he solve his problem according to the text?
options: By taking in more fresh air.
items.exp: 文中说最常见的疗法是接受明亮的人工光照。

items.stem: Why is the sentence “Why do we love sunshine?” written in the last paragraph?
options: To encourage readers to learn more about sunlight.
To advise readers to stay in houses for enough time.
To expect readers to realize the importance of Vitamin D.
To invite readers to walk into nature to enjoy the fresh air.
items.exp: 末句设问鼓励读者继续探索阳光的科学。

sections.title: 克服拖延（五选五）
sections.passage: Putting things off is something a lot of students are troubled with. Between schoolwork, after-school activities and everyday worries, there are too many things you have to deal with every day. (36) You might start falling behind and your grades might get lower. One smart way to fight back is to break big tasks into tiny pieces. Huge projects can feel like a mountain. But if you cut them into smaller steps, it will make it less scary (可怕的). (37) Just tell yourself, "Today, I'll choose my topic and write a little. I 'II take care Of more tomorrow." Step by step, it gets done. The "work and rest" way is also a smart choice for being productive. Set a timer for 25 minutes — go all in, full attention. (38) Have some cookies. Walk around. Once you get going, it's easier to keep it up. (39) Put away your MP3 player and any kind of toys. Find a quiet place where you won't get interrupted (打扰) at all. The less noise, the better your brain can lock in. And don't forget to treat yourself. For example, listen to your favorite song, or watch an interesting TV program. These little things keep you going. (40) Finally, you are sure to see the payoff.
choices: Also, stay away from what pulls your attention.
For example, you’ve got to write a five-page paper.
But if you keep putting them off, they can snowball.
Change doesn’t happen overnight, so stick to it every day.

items.exp: 拖延会让任务越积越多，承接任务繁多并引出成绩下降。
用写五页论文举例说明把大任务拆成小步骤。
专注25分钟后休息5分钟，符合劳逸结合。
收起玩具、寻找安静环境，都是远离干扰。
提醒改变不是一夜发生，需要每天坚持。

sections.title: 授人以渔
sections.passage:
A long time ago, there lived two woodcutters called Barry and Kent in a village. Every morning, they went out into the forest and cut wood to sell at a nearby market.
One hot day, the woodcutters were eating their lunch under a tree (41) a beggar (乞丐) came walking towards them.
“My name is Clark, and I’m very (42),” said the beggar, as he walked up to the two woodcutters. “Can you (43) a little of your lunch for me?”
Barry felt great (44) for Clark, and he took from his bag some food that he (45) for later, and wanted to give it to the poor man. But to his surprise, Kent, who was a (46) man too, stopped him from offering the food.
Kent said to Clark, “We both work all day long and we only have enough food to get us through the day. But if you wish, I can lend you my ax (斧子) and (47) you to cut wood. Then you can sell the wood. And you will have a good (48) of buying yourself food.”
Clark looked a bit unhappy because he had been so looking forward to the food. But after a second thought, he took Kent’s ax, and then watched (49) as Kent explained how to cut wood. Clark was (50) at first, but hours later, he began to cut more quickly.
At the end of the day, the three men walked to the market, (51) the wood that they had cut. Very soon, all of their wood was (52).
“Look at this!” Clark said with (53). “It’s amazing! I have never had so much money in my life!”
“You have done well. After all, it was your first (54),” said Kent, and then he took Clark to a shop in the town and helped him (55) an ax.
“Thank you for everything you did for me,” Clark said to Kent and walked away happily.

与后来更快对照，刚开始很慢 slow。

这是第一次尝试 try。

sections.title: 画圣吴道子
sections.passage:
词库：child / travel / year / and / he / at / consider / many / turn / hard
Wu Daozi was one of the greatest of all Chinese artists. He was well-known for (56) own way of painting with excellent skills.
Wu lost his parents when he was a young (57) and he lived a very poor life. The young Wu had to work very (58) to make a living. He began to learn painting not from famous painters (59) that time, but from folk artisans (民间手艺人) in today’s Henan Province.
In order to learn how to paint landscapes (风景), Wu followed a great painter and he (60) to many places with mountains and rivers. After three (61) of learning, he created the so-called shuti of landscape painting. Also, he became the first artist in Chinese art history to (62) landscapes into a new kind of painting.
Besides landscapes, Wu also learned a lot in painting human figures. He was especially good at it (63) developed his special painting skills.
During his lifetime, Wu painted (64) than 300 amazing murals (壁画). No wonder he is (65) as a “Sage of Art” (画圣) in China.

items.exp: his own 表示他自己的。
a young child 表示幼童。
work hard 表示努力工作。
at that time 为固定搭配。
过去游历各地，用 traveled 或 travelled。
three 后用 years。
turn ... into ... 表示把……变成。
并列两个谓语，用 and。
more than 300 表示超过300。
be considered as 表示被视为。

sections.title: 鱼的生活
sections.passage:
The life of a fish
The life of a fish must be good, I feel.
As long (66) you avoid the fishing reel (钓鱼轮).
I would swim all day, in the ocean blue.
I would lie in (67) sun, with nothing to do.
I wouldn’t have homework to do for my school.
I wouldn’t need to worry (68) all of those rules.
There would be no ice cream, no chocolate, no cake.
No playing in the park, no sitting by the lake.
I think I would miss my comfortable bed.
I wouldn’t like (69) sleep in a cave instead.
A life in the ocean (70) not the life for me.
The life of a fish? I’d rather be me!

items.exp: as long as 表示只要。
太阳是独一无二的，用 the sun。
worry about 为固定搭配。
would like to do 表示想要做。
A life 作主语，be 用 is。

sections.prompt: 假设你是李华，准备在毕业典礼合唱 Auld Lang Syne，想找一位搭档。以 The partner I’m looking for 为主题写约100词发言稿：想找男生还是女生；希望对方擅长什么及理由；希望对方有什么性格及理由。不得出现真实姓名和学校。开头：Hello, everyone! I’m looking for a partner to sing the English song Auld Lang Syne with me at the graduation ceremony. 结尾：Thanks for listening!
sections.sample: Hello, everyone! I am looking for a partner to sing the English song Auld Lang Syne with me at the graduation ceremony. To begin with, since I am a girl, I’d like to pair up with a girl. So it will be more convenient for us both. Second, I wish to work with a partner who is good at singing as excellent singing skills can lead to a successful act. Last, it will be perfect if my would-be partner is easy to get along with because there may be disagreements during the preparation. Team up with me if you are the one I am looking for. Let’s create a piece that belongs to you and me, belongs to the class of 2025! Thanks for listening!
sections.exp: 三项要求都要覆盖，理由对应具体要求，用 To begin with、Second、Last 组织。
